text: An orbit that goes around the Earth 8.05 times a day with an eccentricity of 0.25 (the exact 8:1 resonance with the Earth's rotation) is predicted 1.3 km off along its track 7 days after a fit, against 94 to 220 m just either side of it: no part of the model carries that resonance's gravity terms.

On a 7-day arc of an eccentric orbit with drag (Molniya), the record states the drag coefficient to 0.09 % while the fitted value is 0.3 to 0.5 % from the truth: the stated uncertainty is 5 to 7 times too small; its position covariance is honest.

At 690 and 800 km, near orbits that repeat 29 times in 2 days or 57 times in 4 days over the turning Earth, the gravity field above degree 31 adds 35 to 70 m to the error 5 days after a 3-day fit (52 and 113 m against 13 and 20 m without it): the model carries none of those terms.
In low orbit, with only the Earth's flattening on both sides, the predicted orbit sits a constant 3 to 4.5 m too high or too low: the flattening's effect is carried to first order only.
In low orbit the gravity field's short-period terms are carried to degree 16; degrees 17 to 31 leave 5 to 11 m of position error at 690 to 800 km.
